hypothesis: The near-tie band `band = 1e-3 * (span + 1.0)` mixes a relative unit (span) with an absolute length unit (1.0), so the width of the band is not equivariant under a change of the coordinate scale; the band should therefore dominate the rule when the instance is shrunk and vanish when it is enlarged.
findings: Scale non-equivariance is real and monotone in coordinate scale (+48% at 1e-2, +207% at 1e-3).
Corrected 300-step audit (all 50 customers, exact C.py:35 gate mask>=2 & cur!=0): gate rate jumps 1.7% (s=1) -> 67.7% (s=0.01) -> 84.3% (s=0.001) -> 0.7% (s=1000).

band and cap_term act in series (gate x payload): at s=1 effective all-step cap_term/base median is 0 (0 on 98.3% of steps), whereas conditioned on gated steps cap_term/base scales as O(1/s^2) (4-point log-log slope -1.994: 5.69 -> 51929 -> 5.13e+06).
-1e-6*dem scales as O(1/s) (4-point slope -0.979); band/base has hybrid slope -0.542 because it mixes O(1) relative span with O(1/s) absolute 1e-3.

Direct 3-term ablation across 4 scales: C_full spread=206.99% (s=1: 10.9197, s=1e-3: 33.5221); C_rel_band spread=0.40% (s=1: 11.1297); C_no_cap spread=0.18% (s=1: 11.0859, s=1e-3: 11.0661); C_no_dem spread=205.89% (s=1: 10.9197, s=1e-3: 33.4025); C_no_cap_no_dem spread=0.00%.
guidance: Replace the additive constant with a scale-free gate: keep the firing width that is useful on the nominal unit square, but define it relative to the realized score span (for example a fixed multiple of the top-2 base gap, or a relative band whose coefficient is calibrated so that the nominal firing rate stays near 1-2%). Do not simply divide by span with the same 1e-3 coefficient.

verification.reason: Series gate-x-payload mechanism verified by both 300-step gated audit and direct 3-term ablation: dropping cap_term eliminates the 207% collapse completely (C_no_cap), while making band relative suppresses it to 0.39% (C_rel_band) at a +1.92% nominal cost. Prior rev-2 audit had an off-by-one demands bug (49 steps) and ignored C.py:35's gate, overstating nominal cap_term.
verification.next_test: Start real inter-round autonomous search from frozen C/A (not NN) and test scale-invariant dimensionless secondary ranking on both dev and independent multi-scale held-out (n=50/100/200).

adoption_test.design: 2x2 (operations x research finding), two independent replicates, 4 rounds / 24 requests / 120 solver calls per arm, deepseek-flash
adoption_test.shared_suite: 6 instances, frozen C = 10.9197, search seed NN = 12.1150

candidates.note: a1 produced 10 relative_with_epsilon candidates only because its guidance text contained the patch itself

adoption_test.structural_finding: The search seed is NN (baseline_code_sha256 90b23362), not C, so a finding about C's near-tie band cannot be applied to C: every arm rewrote the constructor instead. In a1 the finding carried C's formula, which is the only reason an agent could copy C back and patch it.

revisions.what: Initial 3-term audit had off-by-one demands (49 steps) and ignored C.py:35 gate; superseded by rev 3.
Fixed 50-customer demands indexing and exact C.py:35 gate; ran direct 3-term ablation confirming band (gate) x cap_term (O(1/s^2) payload) series mechanism.

target_rule: algorithm portfolio {nn, savings, dd_load, radial} on crossed CVRP regimes
hypothesis: No single constructive rule dominates across instance regimes, and the regime can be detected from pre-solve features, so an instance-level selector can recover part of the oracle gap.

evidence.portfolio_size_effect: core-4 and extended-6 give identical VBS/SBS; isolate and load_fill never win a single instance

why_invalid: savings used dep[unvisited] + dep[unvisited] - cur[unvisited]: the depot distance entered twice, so the portfolio member was not the rule it was named after
the eccentric regime changed depot position, capacity headroom and demand range together, so the regime label could not be attributed to any one factor

v3_frozen_c_in_pool.portfolio: core+{c} and extended+{c}; the frozen C rule is read from reports/evidence/cvrp_p0_p1_p2_20261107/p0/frozen_code/C.py and hash-checked, never edited

frozen_member.provenance: PoC frozen rule C; objective 10.9197 on the shared 6-instance suite

selection_cost.training: the matrix needs one construct evaluation per portfolio member per training instance
selection_cost.note: retraining is offline; a deployed selector pays one construct run, not the full portfolio

v4_abc_in_pool.portfolio: full_pool = extended + frozen {A, B, C} (all SHA-256 verified)

findings: Widening the pool to frozen A/B/C expands complementarity from 1.63% (core) / 2.05% (+C) to 4.09% (VBS 1223.8026 vs SBS 1273.8205 [b], headroom 50.0179).

Spatial regime split is real: A wins 3/4 uniform cells (uniform mean a=14.4702 < savings=14.5672 < b=14.7222), while B wins all 4/4 clustered cells (clustered mean b=11.8158 < savings=11.9770 < a=12.2906).

Point-estimate selector gains turn positive for the first time in full_pool: pairwise_loo_unweighted +0.94% (95% CI [-0.08%, +1.92%], p=0.0362), ridge_loo +0.81%, pairwise_loo (cost-sensitive) +0.72%.

However, 8-feature LOO/LORO 95% CIs still cross zero and worst_regret worsens from 17.62% to 25.66%, whereas the 1-feature cluster_stump_loo achieves +0.93% (95% CI [+0.07%, +1.81%], p=0.0163) — showing the predictable signal at n=50 is predominantly spatial clustering.

Pure pre-compiled solve times remove AST-parsing confound: savings=0.72ms, a=0.87ms, c=1.02ms, b=1.09ms (C is slightly faster than B in pure solve time; its 2.62ms full eval cost was >50% AST parsing).
guidance: Do not build a universal selector on these features: the honest use of the 1.63% headroom is a fixed rule plus a narrow, capacity-aware fallback, and the report must say the selector result is negative. If selection is revisited, the target has to change from 'pick a rule' to 'pick when to apply a local improvement', because rule choice is already saturated by savings.

verification.why: Adding strong generalized rules A and B unlocks real spatial complementarity (4.09% gap) and positive out-of-fold selector gains (+0.72% to +0.94% LOO; +0.47% to +0.68% LORO), overturning rev-3's negative claim. Yet 8-feature CIs still cross 0 at n=50/96 instances and a 1-feature cluster_tendency stump captures nearly the entire gain.
verification.next_test: Stage 2 multi-scale heterogeneous testbed (n in {50, 100, 200} x spatial x depot x capacity x demand distribution = 288 instances) with Random Forest, cost-sensitive pairwise, Clarke-Wright merge reference, and Leave-One-Scale-Out (LOSO) validation.

revisions.note: 36 instances, three regimes, savings rule mis-implemented; withdrawn.
96 instances, three factors crossed independently, savings corrected; complementarity 1.63%, no selectable structure.
Frozen C rule entered the pool and a pairwise-comparison selector was added: complementarity 1.63%->2.05%, C never becomes the fixed choice, no learned selector beats fixed savings.

Frozen A/B/C added to pool + pure solve timing + paired bootstrap CIs + 1-feature cluster_stump: gap 4.09%, LOO point estimates +0.72%..+0.94% (8-feature 95% CIs cross 0; 1-feature stump captures the uniform-A vs clustered-B split cleanly).
